Both live in the same `Core` package under `Shared/Core/Sources/Core/Observation/`, carry identical parameter labels (`center:subject:onSubscribed:`), and have no restraint markers (`is_test`, `is_mock`, `is_sample_app`, `is_codegen` all false). The sole structural difference is actor isolation implied by the `MainActor` prefix on one type, making a shared internal helper the most targeted fix without coupling production types to test or sample-app semantics.

specifics.proposed_action: Extract the shared initializer body of `AsyncIterator.init(center:subject:onSubscribed:)` into a common internal helper — either a free function or a shared base struct/mixin — inside the `Core` package (e.g., `Shared/Core/Sources/Core/Observation/NotificationMessageSequenceSupport.swift`). Both `AsyncNotificationMessageSequence.AsyncIterator` (in `AsyncMessage.swift:126`) and `MainActorNotificationMessageSequence.AsyncIterator` (in `MainActorMessage.swift:152`) would delegate to this helper, eliminating the near-duplicate body (Jaccard 0.857). Because the two iterator types differ only in actor isolation (`MainActor` vs. unconstrained), the helper should be written as a non-isolated function so both callers can invoke it safely.
specifics.why_no_category_fits: The two records are initializers on nested types (`AsyncIterator`) of two distinct concrete sequence types, not free functions or top-level types. `generic-parameterization` does not cleanly apply because the divergence is actor-isolation, not a type parameter. `extract-to-common` does not apply because both files already live in the same package (`Core`) and the schema requires moving to an upstream package. `default-implementation` does not apply because there is no shared protocol whose extension could host the default. `subclass-lift` does not apply because these are structs/value types, not class hierarchies. The most idiomatic Swift remedy is a shared internal helper function within the same package, which none of the named categories capture precisely.
